checks: At a C1 boundary point the supporting normal is unique. A nonsingleton support face would contain a segment from the point and, by relative openness, an initial nontrivial segment in the patch. The verified same-batch exposure lemma applies at the chosen base and yields a unique ambient maximizer. Taking the outward direction equal to the own unit normal gives positive dot product one.

There are at most 2^N patterns for N fixed closed caps off their planes. Distinct patterns have distinct lifted representatives. Ambient boundaries agree with restricted-plane zero sets at the lifted points. The signed-local-mass hypotheses thus hold jointly, and finite strict cap margins remain valid after O(epsilon) shifts. The positive actual competitors over the same P converge in precisely the topology of the local-minimum assumption.

The signed equality dual uses the same fixed actual critical circuits, full aggregate two-sided slopes, raw mass Q, and signed competitors. Applying it to the union of the representatives gives one probability vector; the weighted sum depends only on the incidence pattern, so it extends to all patch points off the planes. If no patterns are realized, the equality is vacuous and I is nonempty by compactness and upper semicontinuity of depth.

The pairing lemma is applied with nonnegative weights pi_p kappa_pj and nonzero restricted normals. It yields equal sums for the two orientations on each proper restricted plane that meets the patch. The same vector is used throughout; no claim about points on the planes, ambient pairing, or one vector across alternative circuit choices is needed.

A full-boundary patch makes the whole boundary C1 and segment-free. Proper traces are closed and have empty interior in the boundary by transversality; supporting traces are empty or singletons, hence also closed with empty interior. Each proper plane meets the full boundary. At a point off all planes every proper class contributes half its combined weight and each nonproper class has constant zero or one incidence. This proves beta = F_q + P_q/2 without assigning any payment at closed-cap ties.

For a full-boundary deepest fiber every own cap is proper because its restricted plane contains its interior maximizing mark. Its own weights sum to pi_q, so P_q >= pi_q. Nonnegative F_q yields pi_q <= 2 beta; summing only when all deepest fibers have full patches yields 1 <= 2 |I| beta.

For each unit-normal cap, Fubini writes the closed-cap mass at a moving threshold as the integral of section areas, with each threshold plane of d-volume zero. Proper sections have positive continuous area by Brunn–Minkowski concavity. At a support endpoint, strict convexity gives one point, and compactness forces diameters of approaching sections to zero (otherwise a pair of separated limits lies in the endpoint face). For d >= 2 this gives zero area and continuity with the exterior trace. The finite sum of areas is continuous at the old threshold and positive from the own proper section, giving a common positive derivative magnitude on both sides. This works for d = 2 independently of pairing and need not hold at a supporting endpoint for d = 1.
